name: hepatitis A virus cellular receptor 2
pathways: positive regulation of non-canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction

function.text: HAVCR2 encodes hepatitis A virus cellular receptor 2. Annotated molecular activities include transmembrane signaling receptor activity. It participates in positive regulation of non-canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction and defense response to Gram-positive bacterium.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma (autosomal recessive).

somatic.text: The gene appears in specialty educational coverage, but a disease-specific somatic driver relationship has not been assigned in this draft; expression-marker or assay-context mentions are not mutation evidence.

germline_associations.mechanism: Autosomal recessive; definitive GenCC assertion from G2P. Allele-specific mechanism requires review.

function.text: HAVCR2 encodes hepatitis A virus cellular receptor 2. Based in part on similarity, it is a cell surface receptor implicated in modulating innate and adaptive immune responses. Generally accepted to have an inhibiting function. It reports on stimulating functions suggest that the activity may be influenced by the cellular context and/or the respective ligand.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma (autosomal recessive).
